name: ls
summary: List a directory or describe a single file.

params.name: path
params.description: Directory or file to list (default: working dir). Leading ~ ok.

params.name: all
params.description: Include entries starting with a dot.

params.name: long
params.description: Long format: permissions, owner, size, mtime.

params.name: human_readable
params.description: Human-readable sizes (with long).

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recurse into subdirectories. Use sparingly on deep trees.

params.name: sort_by_size
params.description: Sort by size, largest first.

params.name: sort_by_time
params.description: Sort by mtime, newest first.

name: pwd
summary: Show the server's current working directory.

name: largest_files
summary: List the largest files under a directory, ranked by size (top N only). Use this instead of find for 'biggest files' questions.

params.name: dir
params.description: Directory to scan recursively (default: working dir). Leading ~ ok.

params.name: count
params.description: How many largest files to return (default 10, max 100).

name: spotlight_search
summary: Search this Mac with Spotlight (content AND metadata, like the magnifying glass in the menu bar). Use this for 'find that presentation about Q3' or 'the invoice PDF from last month' — questions about a file's meaning or contents, not its exact name. For an exact name/extension/type match use find; to grep inside known files use grep.

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text search terms (e.g. "quarterly report"). Matched against indexed file contents and metadata. Must not begin with '-'.

params.name: dir
params.description: Restrict the search to this directory tree (default: everywhere Spotlight indexes). Leading ~ ok.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of matching paths to return (default 30, max 200).

name: image_info
summary: Report an image's properties — pixel dimensions, format, color space, DPI, and byte size — using macOS's own sips tool. Use this for 'how big is this photo', 'what format/resolution is this image', not the generic file/stat (which only report the file type and size on disk, not the image's pixel dimensions).

params.name: path
params.description: Image file to inspect (PNG, JPEG, HEIC, TIFF, GIF, …). Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

name: convert_image
summary: Convert an image to another format (e.g. HEIC→JPEG, PNG→PDF) with macOS's sips, writing a NEW file and never overwriting the original or any existing file. Staged for confirmation; reversible: undo moves the created file to the Trash.

params.name: source
params.description: Existing image file to convert. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

params.name: destination
params.description: Path of the NEW converted file to create (its extension should match the chosen format, e.g. photo.jpg for jpeg). Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-'. Must not already exist (no overwrite); parent directory must exist.

params.name: format
params.description: Target image format for the new file.

name: resize_image
summary: Resize an image to a new pixel size with macOS's sips, writing a NEW file and never overwriting the original. Provide EXACTLY ONE of width, height, or max_dimension — the unspecified axis scales to preserve the aspect ratio. Staged for confirmation; reversible: undo moves the created file to the Trash.

params.name: source
params.description: Existing image file to resize. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

params.name: destination
params.description: Path of the NEW resized file to create. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-'. Must not already exist (no overwrite); parent directory must exist.

params.name: width
params.description: Resample to this width in pixels (height scales to keep the aspect ratio). Provide exactly one of width, height, or max_dimension. Range 1–20000.

params.name: height
params.description: Resample to this height in pixels (width scales to keep the aspect ratio). Provide exactly one of width, height, or max_dimension. Range 1–20000.

params.name: max_dimension
params.description: Resample so the LONGER side is at most this many pixels (both axes scale to keep the aspect ratio). Provide exactly one of width, height, or max_dimension. Range 1–20000.

name: convert_document
summary: Convert a text document between plain text, HTML, RTF, RTFD, Word (.docx), and OpenDocument (.odt) using macOS's textutil. Writes a NEW file and never overwrites. Staged for confirmation; reversible: undo moves the created file to the Trash. (Note: textutil does not produce PDF; for PDF output use convert_image on an image, or print to PDF.)

params.name: source
params.description: Existing text document to convert. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

params.name: destination
params.description: Path of the NEW converted file to create (its extension should match the chosen format, e.g. notes.html for html). Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-'. Must not already exist (no overwrite); parent directory must exist.

params.name: format
params.description: Target document format for the new file.

name: quicklook_thumbnail
summary: Generate a Quick Look preview image (PNG) of a file — a document, image, or anything Quick Look can render — using macOS's qlmanage. The thumbnail is written into a server-managed temp folder and its path is returned. Runs immediately (no confirmation needed); reversible: undo moves the generated thumbnail folder to the Trash.

params.name: path
params.description: File to render a Quick Look thumbnail for. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

params.name: size
params.description: Maximum thumbnail dimension in pixels (1–2048, default 512). The longer side is scaled to at most this.

name: file
summary: Identify the type of one or more files (e.g. "PNG image data", "ASCII text").

params.name: paths
params.description: One or more files to identify. Leading ~ ok.

name: stat
summary: Show detailed metadata (size, mtime, permissions, owner) for one or more paths.

params.name: paths
params.description: One or more paths to stat. Leading ~ ok.

name: wc
summary: Count lines, words, characters, or bytes in one or more files. Omit paths to count piped input as the non-first stage of a pipeline.

params.name: lines
params.description: Count lines.

params.name: words
params.description: Count words.

params.name: bytes
params.description: Count bytes.

params.name: chars
params.description: Count characters.

params.name: paths
params.description: Files to count. Leading ~ ok. Omit only as a non-first pipeline stage.

name: du
summary: Report disk usage for one or more paths. Set max_depth to 0 for just a per-argument total.

params.name: human_readable
params.description: Human-readable sizes (1.2K, 47M, 3G).

params.name: total
params.description: Add a grand total across all arguments.

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Report entries at most N levels deep. Use 0 for just each argument's total.

params.name: paths
params.description: Directories or files to measure. Leading ~ ok.

name: find
summary: Locate files by name, extension, type, or depth under a directory.

params.name: path
params.description: Root directory to search under. Leading ~ ok.

params.name: name_pattern
params.description: Glob matching the base file name, e.g. *.png.

params.name: iname_pattern
params.description: Case-insensitive name_pattern.

params.name: type
params.description: Restrict to f (file), d (directory), or l (symlink).

params.name: max_depth
params.description: Maximum directory depth to descend.

params.name: min_depth
params.description: Minimum depth before matching begins.

params.name: extensions
params.description: Extensions without the dot, e.g. ["png","jpg"]; OR-combined, case-insensitive.

name: grep
summary: Search files or directories for a regular expression. Binary files are skipped. Omit paths to search piped input as the non-first stage of a pipeline.

params.name: pattern
params.description: Regular expression to search for.

params.name: paths
params.description: Files or directories to search. Leading ~ ok. Omit only as a non-first pipeline stage.

params.name: recursive
params.description: Recurse into directories.

params.name: ignore_case
params.description: Case-insensitive match.

params.name: line_numbers
params.description: Prefix matches with line numbers. On by default unless a summary mode (files_with_matches/count) is set.

params.name: files_with_matches
params.description: List only the names of files containing matches.

params.name: count
params.description: Print only a count of matching lines per file.

params.name: max_count
params.description: Stop after this many matches per file.

params.name: context
params.description: Print N lines of context around each match.

params.name: include
params.description: Restrict a recursive search to files matching this glob.

name: sort
summary: Sort lines of text. Rarely useful standalone (it needs explicit files); its real purpose is ranking another stage's output as part of a pipeline, e.g. ranking find or du results.

params.name: numeric
params.description: Sort numerically, not lexicographically.

params.name: human_numeric
params.description: Sort by human-readable size (1K, 2M, 3G); use to rank du -h output.

params.name: reverse
params.description: Reverse order (largest first with numeric/human_numeric).

params.name: unique
params.description: Output only the first of each set of equal lines.

params.name: key
params.description: Sort key field, e.g. "2,2" for the second whitespace-separated field.

params.name: paths
params.description: Files to sort. Leading ~ ok. Omit only as a non-first pipeline stage (sorts the prior stage's output).

name: head
summary: Show the first N lines (or bytes) of text. Rarely useful standalone; its real purpose is trimming a ranked or filtered pipeline result down to a top-N answer.

params.name: count
params.description: Number of lines to print (default 10 if neither count nor bytes is set).

params.name: bytes
params.description: Number of bytes to print instead of lines. Set at most one of count/bytes.

params.name: paths
params.description: Files to read. Leading ~ ok. Omit only as a non-first pipeline stage (trims the prior stage's output).

name: mkdir
summary: Create a new directory. Reversible: undo removes the created directory (only if still empty).

params.name: path
params.description: Directory to create. Leading ~ ok. Parent must exist; target must not.

name: move
summary: Move (or rename) a file or directory. Reversible: undo moves it back to its original location. To move many files at once, use source_glob instead of source.

params.name: source
params.description: Single existing file or directory to move. Provide exactly one of source or source_glob. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

params.name: source_glob
params.description: Shell glob selecting MANY files to move (e.g. ~/Desktop/Screenshot*.png). The server expands it on disk, so filenames with characters you can't type (like the narrow no-break space in macOS screenshot names) are matched reliably. All matches must share one parent directory, and destination must be an existing directory. Provide exactly one of source or source_glob.

params.name: destination
params.description: Target path. Leading ~ ok. With source: into an existing dir → placed inside under its name, else it is the new path. With source_glob: must be an existing directory. Must not already exist for any item (no overwrite); parent dir must exist.

name: copy
summary: Copy a file or directory (recursive). Reversible: undo moves the new copy to the Trash.

params.name: source
params.description: Existing file or directory to copy. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

params.name: destination
params.description: Target path. Leading ~ ok. Into an existing dir → placed inside under the source's name; else it is the new path. Must not already exist (no overwrite); parent dir must exist.

name: remove
summary: Delete a file or directory by moving it to the Trash (never a hard delete). Reversible: undo restores it from the Trash.

params.name: path
params.description: Existing file or directory to send to the Trash. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

name: write_file
summary: Create a NEW text file with the given content (never overwrites an existing file). Reversible: undo moves the created file to the Trash.

params.name: path
params.description: Path of the file to create. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./). Parent directory must exist; target must not.

params.name: content
params.description: Full text content of the new file (may be empty for an empty file; max 1 MiB). Delivered to the file verbatim as data — never parsed as flags or code.

name: append_to_file
summary: Append text to an EXISTING file. Reversible: undo restores the file's prior contents byte-for-byte.

params.name: path
params.description: Existing regular file to append to (max 8 MiB — undo stores the prior contents). Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

params.name: content
params.description: Text to append (max 1 MiB, not empty). Delivered verbatim as data; include a leading newline yourself if the file should end its current line first.

name: compress
summary: Create a .zip, .tar.gz, or .tgz archive from one or more files/folders. Staged for confirmation; reversible: undo moves the created archive to the Trash.

params.name: archive
params.description: Path of the archive to create. Must end in .zip, .tar.gz, or .tgz — the extension picks the format. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./). Must not already exist; its parent directory must exist and must not sit inside anything being compressed.

params.name: sources
params.description: One or more existing files/folders to put in the archive. All must share one parent directory (their names are stored relative to it, e.g. 'project/report.txt'). Leading ~ ok; none may start with '-' (use ./).

name: extract
summary: Extract a .zip, .tar.gz, or .tgz archive into an existing EMPTY directory. Nothing can be written outside the destination (no zip-slip): a member with a '..' path is refused, and an absolute member has its leading '/' stripped so it lands inside. Staged for confirmation; reversible: undo moves the destination — with everything unpacked into it — to the Trash.

params.name: archive
params.description: Existing .zip, .tar.gz, or .tgz archive to unpack. Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).

params.name: destination
params.description: Existing EMPTY directory to unpack into (create it first with mkdir). Leading ~ ok; must not start with '-' (use ./).
